quotes.why: The verse the paragraph gives to རྗེ་བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ, found in Tsongkhapa's own collected works as the refuge stanza of a short verse exhortation; it reads གཅིག་པུར་ཀུན་ཏ་འཁྱམས་པ and སྐྱབས་གཞན་མེད where the yig cha has གཅིག་པུ་ཀུན་ཏུ་རྒྱུ་བ and སྐྱབས་གནས་མེད. Found by direct search.
The colophon of the same short work, naming Lobsang Drakpa as author: it is what settles that རྗེ་བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ here means Tsongkhapa. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Sungbum/PHAR PHYIN_PERFECTION OF WISDOM (PRAJNA PARAMITA) (MADHYAMIKA SVATANTRIKA SCHOOL)/SPYI_GENERAL COMMENTARIES/KUN MKHYEN CHOS 'BYOR DPAL BZANG_KUNKYEN CHUNJOR PELSANG/S00999E_BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN 'GREL PA 'GREL BSHAD DANG BCAS PA'I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA BSAM 'PHEL DBANG GI RGYAL PO_'The Lord of Lords among Wish-Giving Gems,' being a Detailed Commentary to both the Commentary and Subcommentary _unicode.txt
quotes.why: A near-verbatim twin of the paragraph's first half in another Abhisamayālaṃkāra commentary: same heading, same three trainings, same reason — but 'not even in a dream' where the yig cha has 'not even for an instant'. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Sungbum/PHAR PHYIN_PERFECTION OF WISDOM (PRAJNA PARAMITA) (MADHYAMIKA SVATANTRIKA SCHOOL)/SPYI_GENERAL COMMENTARIES/KUN MKHYEN CHOS 'BYOR DPAL BZANG_KUNKYEN CHUNJOR PELSANG/S00999E_BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN 'GREL PA 'GREL BSHAD DANG BCAS PA'I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA BSAM 'PHEL DBANG GI RGYAL PO_'The Lord of Lords among Wish-Giving Gems,' being a Detailed Commentary to both the Commentary and Subcommentary _unicode.txt
quotes.why: The same verse in the twin passage, with Tsongkhapa's reading སྐྱབས་གཞན་མེད and introduced as spoken by བརྩེ་བ་ཆེན་པོ rather than རྗེ་བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ. Found by direct search.

quotes.text: ལྔ་པ་ལ། སོ་སོའི་བསླབ་བྱ་དང་། ཐུན་མོང་བའི་བསླབ་བྱ་གཉིས་ལས། དང་པོ་ལ། དགག་པའི་བསླབ་བྱ་དང་། སྒྲུབ་པའི་བསླབ་བྱ་གཉིས་ལས།
quotes.why: The division that the paragraph's opening གཉིས་པ་ནི answers to: the refuge trainings split into specific and common, and this paragraph gives the common ones.
The root verse on the ten instructions: the paragraph closes the commentary on its second line (the Three Jewels) and opens the commentary on the first item of its third line, མ་ཞེན.
Haribhadra's whole gloss on མ་ཞེན: it names exertion and a clinging to the བསོད་ནམས of body and the rest, but says nothing of laziness or of Śāntideva's three kinds — that mapping is Tibetan.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 3 (GA)/TD03790-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA (Pañca Viṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The sentence the yig cha quotes as the jumping-off point, with Haribhadra's own section-marker དགེ་འདུན་དཀོན་མཆོག་ལ་གདམས་པའོ written into his rearranged sūtra — which is why the yig cha can say 'in the context of the instruction on the Saṅgha Jewel'.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 3 (GA)/TD03790-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA (Pañca Viṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The Buddha's answer as the yig cha quotes it, in the recension it actually follows: the fault is the thought that there is a body, speech and mind by which one undertakes the action. The yig cha reads བརྩོན་པ where this has རྩོམ་པ.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The same answer in the Kangyur's unrearranged Pañcaviṃśati, worded differently ('this is the body; by it let me undertake a bodily action') — showing the yig cha's wording comes from Haribhadra's edition, not this one.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 3 (GA)/TD03790-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA (Pañca Viṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Where the quoted sūtra span ends in Haribhadra's edition, with his marker 'this is the instruction on non-attachment'; the yig cha's closing words ཐུབ་པར་དཀའ་བ stand where this reads ཐུབ་པར་མི་ནུས.

An Indian commentator on the Śatasāhasrikā saying outright that ཁ་ན་མ་ཐོ་བ here does not mean unwholesome deeds but objectifying activity of body, speech and mind — the key to the sūtra the paragraph quotes.
Tsongkhapa introducing the three-exertions-against-three-lazinesses reading of this line of the Ornament, and naming the first laziness སྙོམས་ལས་འཛིན་པ. Found by direct search.
Tsongkhapa reads Haribhadra's term as བསོད་ཉམས and glosses it as the pleasure that arises — the reading Chökyi Gyaltsen follows in the next paragraph. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/04 DBU MA_Middle Way School (Madhyamaka)/VOL 10 (LA)/TD03871_BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SPYOD PA LA 'JUG PA (Bodhisattva Caryāvatāra)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Śāntideva's own line on the adverse side of exertion, which the Tibetan commentaries map onto the Ornament's three instructions.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's own outline of this same line, earlier in this text, naming the laziness སྙོམས་ལས་འཛིན་པ as Tsongkhapa does — where the paragraph itself says བྱ་བ་ངན་ཞེན. Found by direct search.
Khedrup Je naming the laziness here བྱ་བ་ངན་ཞེན — the label the paragraph uses — and explaining it as attachment to ordinary bodily pleasure. Found by direct search.

Gyaltsab Je treating the same sūtra as instruction not to cling to bad activity, by realising that body and the rest lack own-nature ultimately — the doctrinal content the next paragraph draws out. Found by direct search.
